sections.title: Hotel threat profile
paragraphs: Rush is a fast passing threat in DOORS, the Roblox experience made by LSPLASH. This dossier covers ordinary Hotel runs. Its purpose is to help identify a warning and choose shelter, not to promise a fixed spawn at a particular door. Event modes and later floors need their own rules and should not inherit a Hotel timing guide unchanged.

sections.title: Read the approach
paragraphs: Flickering lights can warn that Rush is approaching, and its sound becomes an important cue. Rush can break room lights as it passes, leaving later exploration darker. The Greenhouse has different lighting conditions, so a plan based only on a visible flicker is incomplete. Locate usable shelter before becoming absorbed in drawers, keys or another screen.

sections.title: Shelter, listen, then move
paragraphs: Get into a valid hiding place before the passage reaches you, then listen for the danger to clear. Avoid leaving just to inspect the monster. GameBreak’s suggested practice is to identify the nearest shelter each time you enter a room; this reduces decision time when a warning arrives. It is a practice suggestion, not a tested guarantee of survival.

sections.title: Hide is a second timer
paragraphs: Remaining hidden too long can bring Hide into the encounter and force you out. Pay attention to its warning while also tracking Rush outside. The available hiding time changes with context and modifiers; copying one countdown from an old video can fail. Ambush is a different encounter with returning passes, so do not treat every rushing sound as identical.

history.label: A floor-specific change
history.detail: The community history records forward-origin attacks added for The Mines in August 2024. That history is a reason to keep Hotel and Mines instructions separate, not evidence that every Hotel attack comes from ahead.

sections.title: Two Hotel objectives
paragraphs: Figure patrols key Hotel encounters, including the Library and the Electrical Room. Treat it as an obstacle while completing the room’s objective, rather than a normal enemy with an invented health bar. This reference covers standard Hotel play; Mines encounters and special modes can change the route, distractions and required actions.

sections.title: Sound and distance
paragraphs: Figure reacts to sound and close proximity. Crouching near it helps reduce the chance of attracting attention, but does not make contact safe. Keep space, watch its movement and avoid crossing its path merely because you are crouched. If it approaches your hiding place, follow the on-screen encounter prompts instead of assuming every wardrobe is unconditional protection.

sections.title: Solve the Library while moving safely
paragraphs: Collect the marked books to reveal symbol–number pairs, then use the Solution Paper to place the needed numbers in order. Enter that sequence at the exit lock. GameBreak suggests separating the task into observe, collect and decode: pause the search when Figure blocks a route, and check your recorded pairs before moving to the lock.

sections.title: Temporary help is not a defeat
paragraphs: A Crucifix only restrains Figure temporarily; it does not permanently banish this boss. Use the pause to reposition rather than waiting beside the chains. Old footage may show safe corners or different behavior that no longer matches the room. Once the exit objective is complete, prioritize leaving instead of returning for optional loot near Figure.

history.label: The Mines update, August 2024
history.detail: The community history documents changes to Figure’s AI, animations and hit detection. This explains why older routes should be checked against the current encounter rather than labeled permanently safe.

sections.title: Spend a tool to skip a key search
paragraphs: A Lockpick opens supported ordinary locks without finding the matching key. Equip it at the locked object and complete the interaction. It is consumed when used, so the useful question is not simply whether the door can be opened, but whether skipping this search is worth losing a tool that might help later.

sections.title: Find or buy in the Hotel
paragraphs: The community reference lists containers, the Pre-Run Shop and Jeff Shop as Hotel sources. Check what is actually offered in your run rather than expecting a specific purchase to appear. GameBreak suggests counting the tools you already hold before shopping, then deciding which upcoming locked objective you intend to reserve one for.

sections.title: Locks it does and does not solve
paragraphs: Lockpicks can open ordinary locked doors and supported locked containers. They cannot substitute for the Library’s combination puzzle or open skeleton-locked doors by themselves. The community article also records generator use in The Mines, which is a separate floor mechanic. Do not read that extra function as a reason to insert the tool into every Hotel object.

sections.title: Time saved versus resources spent
paragraphs: GameBreak’s planning suggestion is to search an easy, well-understood room normally and consider a Lockpick when searching is taking attention away from survival. A tool does not identify the correct exit for you. Track room numbers and the objective first; opening the wrong route quickly is still a mistake. This advice has been source reviewed, not tested in your run settings.
